entries.body: The second number: on notes, asides, and the space beside the text.
entries.title: Notes from the Margin

entries.author: A. Novak
entries.body:
The grid was rigid, and the margins were wide.[^1] Every page of the 1971 Brno catalogue left a third of its width empty,{>> cf. Gerstner, *Designing Programmes*, 1964 <<} and the emptiness was not waste.

A footnote sends the reader down and back up again.[^2] A margin note stays beside the line it belongs to,{>> Tufte's sidenotes are the modern descendant. <<} so the eye only moves sideways.

Příliš žluťoučký kůň úpěl ďábelské ódy, as the type specimens of the period liked to say.[^3] The sentence tests every diacritic a Czech text needs, and it tested the margins too: a long accented line is the first to run into them.{>> Polish specimens did the same with *Zażółć gęślą jaźń*. <<}

[^1]: Brno, 1971.
[^2]: Like this one.
[^3]: "Too yellow a horse moaned devilish odes."
entries.dek: The margin is where the book talks back.

entries.title: Margins and Grids

entries.author: A. Novak
entries.body:
A printed page asks to be read at its own pace. The measure, the leading and the width of the margin all set a tempo before a single word is understood.[^1]

The scholarly books of the early seventies knew this. They gave the text room, and they trusted the reader to stay.

[^1]: The same is true on a screen, though screens rarely admit it.
entries.dek: A defence of the long line and the patient reader.

entries.author: J. Kral
entries.body: A grid is a promise made to the reader: things of the same kind will be found in the same place. Keep the promise and the reader stops searching and starts reading.
entries.dek: Why a strict grid frees the designer instead of binding them.

entries.body:
*The Quarterly* is published four times a year, in numbered issues.

Text is set in **Archivo**, by Omnibus-Type; folios and labels in **IBM Plex Mono**, by IBM. Both are used under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, whose texts ship with this site in `/fonts/`.

Images are printed as black-and-white plates. The site is built with biblio.
